messages.subject: multivariate multilevel model, extremely slow
parts:
Hi all

i have a multilevel multivariate model, where the dependent variables are correlated, also the predictor parameters withing each dependent variable are correlated.

The code that is attach has an example (with simulated data) that converged and gives correct parameter results.

The problem is that to converged it requires 2000 iteration (with 4 chains), and these takes 24 hours.

I am also including the stan code here.

I have tried to implement the recomendations to speed up my code, by vectorizing. Is there something i could do to make this work faster?


thank you


model::

data{
int n; // number or rows
int parmt; // number of parameters estimated
int nsubj; // number of subjects
int nvars; // number of dependent variables  
vector[nvars] y[n]; // matrix of order y[n,nvars], dependent variables
int id[n]; // vector with the id at each row
real x[n]; // vector of time, independent variable
vector[parmt] pm[nvars]; //array with mean priors for multi_normal of mub, of order [nvars,parmt]
cov_matrix[parmt] cov_vb; // covariance with priors for multi_normal of mub
cov_matrix[nvars] cov_vm; // covariance with priors for multi_normal of mu
vector[nvars] mm; // vector with prior means of mu
}

parameters {
vector[parmt] b[nvars,nsubj]; // array of order b[nvars,nsubj,parmt], 1 matrix [nsubj,parmt] for each dependent variable
vector[parmt] mub[nvars]; // array of order mub[nvars,parmt]
corr_matrix[parmt] Sigma_corr_b[nvars]; // array of correlation matrices, one for each dependent variable, of b's
corr_matrix[nvars] Sigma_corr_y; // correlation matrix between dependent variables
vector<lower=0>[parmt] Sigma_sd_b[nvars]; // array of standard deviations for the b's
vector<lower=0>[nvars] Sigma_sd_y; // standard deviations of the dependent variables
}

transformed parameters {
cov_matrix[parmt] Sigma_b[nvars]; // array of covariance matrices of b's, one for each dependent variable
cov_matrix[nvars] Sigma_y; // covariance of dependent variables

for (m in 1:parmt) {
for (j in 1:nvars){
Sigma_b[j,m,m] <- Sigma_sd_b[j,m] * Sigma_sd_b[j,m] * Sigma_corr_b[j,m,m];
for (k in (m+1):parmt) {
Sigma_b[j,m,k] <- Sigma_sd_b[j,m] * Sigma_sd_b[j,k] * Sigma_corr_b[j,m,k];
Sigma_b[j,k,m] <- Sigma_b[j,m,k];
}}}

for (m in 1:nvars) {
Sigma_y[m,m] <- Sigma_sd_y[m] * Sigma_sd_y[m] * Sigma_corr_y[m,m];
for (k in (m+1):nvars) {
Sigma_y[m,k] <- Sigma_sd_y[m] * Sigma_sd_y[k] * Sigma_corr_y[m,k];
Sigma_y[k,m] <- Sigma_y[m,k];
}}

}

model{

for (k in 1:nvars){
Sigma_corr_b[k] ~ lkj_corr(2.0);} // prior for covariance of b's

Sigma_corr_y ~ lkj_corr(2.0); // prior for covariance of dependent variables

for (j in 1:nsubj){
for (k in 1:nvars){
b[k,j] ~ multi_normal(mub[k], Sigma_b[k]);}}

{ // change-point regression
vector[nvars] mu[n]; // local vector of order mu[n,nvars]
for (i in 1:n){
for (k in 1:nvars){
mu[i,k] <- b[k,id[i],1] + b[k,id[i],2] * x[i];
if (x[i] > b[k,id[i],4])
mu[i,k] <- mu[i,k] + (b[k,id[i],3] * (x[i] - b[k,id[i],4]));
}

y[i] ~ multi_normal(mu[i], Sigma_y);

mu[i] ~ multi_normal(mm, cov_vm);
}
}

for (k in 1:nvars){
mub[k] ~ multi_normal(pm[k], cov_vb);}

}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] multivariate multilevel model, extremely slow
parts:
On 10/24/13 11:33 AM, Mauricio Garnier-Villarreal wrote:
> I have tried to implement the recomendations to speed up my code,
> by vectorizing. Is there something i could do to make
> this work faster?
One thing you could do is that because these:

for (i in 1:n){
for (k in 1:nvars){
mu[i,k] <- b[k,id[i],1] + b[k,id[i],2] * x[i];
if (x[i] > b[k,id[i],4])
mu[i,k] <- mu[i,k] + (b[k,id[i],3] * (x[i] - b[k,id[i],4]));
}

y[i] ~ multi_normal(mu[i], Sigma_y);

mu[i] ~ multi_normal(mm, cov_vm);

wind up using the same covariance matrices Sigma_y and cov_vm
for every i, you could vectorize further by creating a single vector
concateaning all the y[i] and mu[i] together. (You don't want
to do both.)

For instance, the second loop can be rewritten more efficiently
using a couple local vectors as:

{
vector[k * n] mubs;
vector[k * n] pms;
int pos;
pos <- 1;

for (j in 1:parmt) {
mubs[pos] <- mub[k,j];
pms[pos] <- pm[k,j];
pos <- pos + 1;
}
}
mubs ~ multi_normal(pms,cov_vb);
}

This way the linear algebra factoring cov_vb only happens once,
not k times.

Or you could Cholesky factor the covariance matrix and use the Cholesky factor in a
call to multi_normal_cholesky. This is neater, but not quite as
efficient. (You don't need to do both.)

Also, you should use Stan 1.3 until we roll out 2.0.1 (later
today or tomorrow). Version 2.0.0 has a bug in
the multivariate normal gradient calc that slows down
computation by making proposals less efficient (you'll still
get the right answer, just more slowly). We're about to
roll out the fix for that later today or tomorrow.

I'm sorry to say we've mainly worked on accelerating the
non-multivariate models. We are working on several things
to make the multi-variate models faster in the future:

1. correlation matrix Cholesky factor type: this will let you
code the whole model more efficiently using this type.

2. analytic gradients for multivariate transform: this will
speed up your existing model and also the one we'll do for
the Cholesky factor

3. analytic gradients for multivariate normal: this will also
speed up all models using multivariate normals

4. multiplication function to scale covariance matrix by a vector
with analytic gradients

These should provide more than an order of magnitude speedup for
the kinds of models you're looking at (and Gaussian process models).
They're pretty high priority for us at this point, but it'll probably
be a few quarters until we're ready to release.

- Bob
